newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end weaker but outperform on dollar.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end weaker but outperform on dollar.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Thursday, pulled lower by weakness in U.S. treasuries, but outperformed U.S. issues amid steady trade in the Canadian dollar, analysts said.

"Canada seemed to have held in very well," said Mary Jane Yule, a senior fixed income portfolio manager with Jones Heward Investment Counsel Inc. "Part of that is the dollar staying relatively stable in the low C$1.39 area."
Canada's 30-year benchmark fell C$0.25 to C$108.05 to yield 7.304 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond fell 15/32 to yield 7.12 percent.
The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 18 basis points from 20 basis points at the close of trading.

Canadian bonds ended lower with U.S. Treasuries, which were hurt by an influx of government and corporate supply and comments by Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer. Meyer said in a speech that the U.S. economy appears to be growing at an unsustainable above-trend rate.
"That seems to have put some pressure on the market, but Treasuries were down in the morning as well," said Yule.

The Canadian dollar did help cushion losses in Canada, analysts said. The currency traded as strong as C$1.3909 (US$0.719) during the session, after strengthening yesterday on comments from Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen.
Dealers said trading in both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets is expected to remain light until next week, when key reports on U.S. employment costs and employment growth will be released.
In other prices, the Canadian 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.18 to C$101.70 to yield 6.754 percent. The U.S. bond fell 11/32 to yield 6.93 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 18 basis points from 15 basis points at Wednesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.15 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.29 percent.
